# The RBI draft model-risk guidance, and what a warrant supplies

<!-- Generated by controlplane/report/crosswalk.py. Do not edit by hand; tests/test_crosswalk.py fails if this page differs from the register. -->

**Source.** Reserve Bank of India, *Guidance on Regulatory Principles for Model Risk Management, 2026*. **DRAFT for public consultation; no final text as of the read date.** Released 2026-06-24; comments closed 2026-07-24; read on 2026-09-14. [Document](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/bs_viewcontent.aspx?Id=5089), [press release](https://www.rbi.org.in/scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=63006).

**This is not a compliance claim.** Each row says what kind of evidence this repository produces toward one paragraph, which code produces it, which test holds it, and what it does not do. Paragraph numbers are the draft's and may move in the final text.

**What the draft does not ask, and a warrant adds.** The draft requires validation and monitoring and sets no evidential standard for either: no confidence level, no sample size, nothing about a validation the data cannot support. A warrant states every rate with an interval and its n, refuses when the evidence cannot support the budget, and prices what re-validation costs (`warrant plan`).

20 paragraphs: 2 provided, 13 partial, 5 not provided.

## ¶51 -- Third-party model that does not disclose: PROVIDES

> the RE should identify risks that arise from such constraints, and put in place the necessary mitigants, such as limiting the usage

## ¶21 -- Inventory; nothing used unless inventoried: PARTIAL

> It should ensure that no model is used, relied upon, or deployed unless it is part of inventory.

**Code:** `controlplane/matrix/matrix.py::WarrantMatrix`, `controlplane/policy/resolution.py::resolve_bundle`

**Held by:** `tests/test_matrix.py::test_unvalidated_routes_conservatively_and_enqueues`, `tests/test_policy.py::test_a_bundle_relying_on_no_warrant_is_refused`

**Does not:** The matrix is an inventory of warrants -- detector by evaluation set -- and an unvalidated cell is routed conservatively rather than relied on. It is not a model inventory: no owner, risk tier, or inactive and decommissioned states.

## ¶29 -- Independent validation, third-party models included: PARTIAL

> An RE should ensure that all models, including third-party models, are subject to independent validation by the RE.

**Code:** `controlplane/intake/certify.py::certify_items`, `controlplane/validation/issuance.py::issue_or_refuse`

**Held by:** `tests/test_intake.py::test_insufficient_evidence_is_a_refusal`, `tests/test_intake.py::test_the_bound_is_respected_on_the_supplied_negatives`, `tests/test_validation.py::test_no_override`

**Evidence:** `results/warrant_matrix.md`, `results/external/MATRIX.md`

**Does not:** Validates detectors and classifiers that emit a score or a verdict -- a PII detector, a hallucination trigger, an injection classifier -- against a false-positive budget on a declared evaluation set. It does not validate the generative model those detectors guard.

**Note:** certify reads only id, label and score, so a vendor's detector is validated without its weights or its cooperation.

## ¶30 -- When validation happens: PARTIAL

> prior to and after deployment of a model, following modification, on internal or external triggers, and periodically as specified in the MRMF

**Code:** `controlplane/intake/certify.py::certify_items`, `controlplane/intake/recheck.py::recheck_items`, `controlplane/drift/response.py::respond_to_drift`, `controlplane/drift/model_version.py::invalidate_for_model_change`

**Held by:** `tests/test_recheck.py::test_a_broken_bound_revokes`, `tests/test_model_version.py::test_an_activation_warrant_on_a_changed_model_is_revoked`, `tests/test_revocation_trace.py::test_the_committed_trace_meets_every_preregistered_criterion`

**Evidence:** `results/drift/revocation_trace.json`

**Does not:** Nothing schedules periodic validation: `warrant plan` prices a cadence and the entity's framework sets it. A modification is detected by model pin for activation-tier warrants only; a vendor detector that changes behind an unchanged name is caught only by a recheck on fresh labels.

## ¶31 -- What validation assesses: PARTIAL

## ¶37 -- Ongoing monitoring of deployed models: PARTIAL

> All deployed models, including third-party models, should be subject to ongoing monitoring, to ensure alignment with the intended outcomes.

**Code:** `controlplane/intake/recheck.py::recheck_items`, `controlplane/drift/monitor.py::DriftMonitor`, `controlplane/economics/sizing.py::monitoring_plan`

**Held by:** `tests/test_drift.py::test_a_real_shift_revokes`, `tests/test_recheck.py::test_a_broken_bound_revokes`, `tests/test_recheck_power.py::test_c2_the_planned_power_is_what_recheck_actually_delivers`

**Evidence:** `results/drift/revocation_trace.json`

**Does not:** Drift is computed on input token length and on the score distribution only; four declared features and MMD are not built. No production traffic has been monitored. A schedule of fixed-size rechecks revokes a sound detector more often the more often it runs, and `warrant plan` states by how much rather than preventing it.

## ¶54(2) -- Hallucination control boundaries: PARTIAL

> put in place appropriate control boundaries through system-level controls or model design features to mitigate risks of hallucinations

**Code:** `controlplane/gate/gate.py::decide`, `controlplane/matrix/matrix.py::WarrantMatrix`

**Held by:** `tests/test_gate.py::test_an_injected_instruction_passes_every_check_and_is_blocked_anyway`, `tests/test_matrix.py::test_unvalidated_routes_conservatively_and_enqueues`

**Evidence:** `results/warrant_matrix.md`, `results/gate/GATE.md`

**Does not:** The warranted hallucination detector bounds how often an expensive check is triggered, at a measured recall that is low on the measured evaluation set (README claim table). It does not bound how often a hallucination reaches a customer. The action gate's first two rules consult no detector.

## ¶54(7) -- Data drift and concept drift: PARTIAL

> Changes in data distribution, including data drift and concept drift, should be monitored and addressed on an ongoing basis.

**Code:** `controlplane/drift/monitor.py::DriftMonitor`, `controlplane/intake/recheck.py::recheck_items`

**Held by:** `tests/test_drift.py::test_a_real_shift_revokes`, `tests/test_drift.py::test_a_configuration_that_alarms_on_its_own_reference_is_refused`

**Evidence:** `results/drift/revocation_trace.json`

**Does not:** Data drift: PSI against a null band simulated at the sample's own size, on one input feature and the score distribution. Concept drift -- the same inputs, different correct labels -- is visible only through a recheck on fresh labels, whose cost `warrant plan` states.

## ¶60(ii) -- Override, suspension, kill switch: PARTIAL

> override, suspension, or deactivation mechanisms, including kill-switch arrangements

**Code:** `controlplane/model/override.py::OverrideRecord`, `controlplane/drift/response.py::respond_to_drift`

**Held by:** `tests/test_override.py::test_a_record_without_a_stratum_cannot_be_built`, `tests/test_override.py::test_an_unweighted_record_cannot_reach_the_ledger`, `tests/test_drift_response.py::test_a_revocation_routes_and_adopts_the_new_bounds`

**Does not:** A human override of an escalated item is recorded, and a revoked warrant suspends the routes relying on it. There is no serving layer, so a kill switch belongs to the entity's gateway.

**Note:** These override a model's outputs. A warrant's refusal has no override (CLAUDE.md invariant 3); the two are different objects, and the paragraph asks for the first.

## ¶33 -- Validation reports to the risk committee: NOT PROVIDED

> Validation reports, including key findings, and recommendations, should be placed before RMCB

**Does not:** A governance process. The warrant record, the matrix and RESULTS.md are inputs a validation report can cite; nothing here writes or files one.

## ¶34 -- Exception approval: NOT PROVIDED

> an approval structure, including exception approval that, inter alia, covers approval authorities, thresholds, additional requirements for models approved with exceptions, and remediation timelines

**Does not:** Nothing records a deployment approved with an exception beside a REFUSED warrant. Whether the product should, without letting an exception read as a warrant, is OPEN (DECISIONS.md 189).

## ¶54(1)(i) -- Explainability thresholds: NOT PROVIDED

> It should define the explainability and transparency thresholds for all AI models

**Does not:** No explainability is measured. The activation probe is a correlational classifier and is documented as explaining nothing about why a model answered as it did.

## ¶54(3) -- Bias and fairness assessment: NOT PROVIDED

> it should conduct fairness assessment and implement appropriate mitigants

**Does not:** Not built. A per-response bias score is out of scope as unsound (CLAUDE.md), and the cohort path that would replace it does not exist.

## ¶55 -- Red-teaming: NOT PROVIDED

> structured challenge processes, including red-teaming or equivalent testing

**Does not:** No red-teaming and no adversarial-robustness claim. The gate's injection result is one declared scenario (reports/PHASE-6.md), not a challenge process.
